# India {background-image="https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/1920px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail" background-size="30%" background-position="85% 50%"}

## The National Insignia {background-image="https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Emblem_of_India.svg/960px-Emblem_of_India.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail" background-size="25%" background-position="95% 50%"}

> National Emblem


::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%"}

- Lion Capital of Ashoka, Sarnath (MP).

- Adopted as the state emblem of India: 26 Jan 1950, the day when India became a Republic.

- *Satyameva Jayate* from *Mundaka Upanishad*. It is national motto.

:::

::: {.column}

:::

:::

::: aside
Insignia = चिह्न अधिचिह्न
:::

## The Ashoka Pillar {background-image="https://culturalsamvaad.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Conjectural-View-of-Sarnath-Lion-Capital-e1685285953823-668x1024.jpg" background-size="contain" background-position="right"}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="68%"}

- Capital means top of a pillar, around 7 feet tall on a 50-40 feet tall pillar, at Sarnath.

- Sarnath (MP) where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

- Ashoka, an emperor of Maurya Empire placed pillars like this one at several Buddhist monasteries.

::: 

::: 

::: {.footer}
Information from [UC Berkeley](https://orias.berkeley.edu/lion-capital-ashoka) & image from [Cultural Samvad](https://culturalsamvaad.com/sarnath-lion-capital-from-an-ashokan-pillar-to-indias-state-emblem/)
:::

## The Capital {background-image="https://orias.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/styles/openberkeley_image_full/public/general/day1-1-sarnath_capital_with_numbers.jpg?itok=2t7brxs4&timestamp=1682567623" background-size="contain" background-position="right" .scrollable} 

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="70%" .r-fit-text}

1. The entire piece was the capital. 

1. Horizontal disk is called abacus, it sits between the capital and the pillar.

1. Dharmachakra (Wheel of Law), in Buddhism dharma means the universal law that governs the universe.

1. Four lions on the capital, four cardinal direction, also Buddha, also Ashoka.

1. The abacus has 4 wheels on it, also representing the dharmachakra. 

1. In between the wheels are four animals: an elephant, a bull, a horse, and a lion. These animals were all associated with Buddhism.

1. The bottom of the capital is a lotus.


::: 

::: 

::: {.footer}
Information and image from [UC Berkeley](https://orias.berkeley.edu/lion-capital-ashoka)
:::

## National Anthem

> "Jana Gana Mana"


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Author & Composer: Rabindranath Tagore

- Year Composed: 1911

- Official Adoption Date: January 24, 1950

:::

::: {.column .r-fit-text}

जनगणमन-अधिनायक जय हे भारतभाग्यविधाता!

पंजाब सिंध गुजरात मराठा द्राविड़ उत्कल बंग

विंध्य हिमाचल यमुना गंगा उच्छलजलधितरंग

तव शुभ नामे जागे, तव शुभ आशिष मागेे,

गाहे तव जयगाथा।

जनगणमंगलदायक जय हे भारतभाग्यविधाता!

जय हे, जय हे, जय हे, जय जय जय जय हे॥

:::

:::


## National Song

> "Vande Mataram"


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Author & Composer: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee

- Year Published: 1882

- Official Adoption Date: January 24, 1950

:::

::: {.column .r-fit-text}

वन्दे मातरम्।

सुजलाम् सुफलाम् मलय़जशीतलाम्,

शस्यश्यामलाम् मातरम्। वन्दे मातरम्।

शुभ्रज्योत्स्ना पुलकितयामिनीम्,

फुल्लकुसुमित द्रुमदलशोभिनीम्,

सुहासिनीम् सुमधुरभाषिणीम्,

सुखदाम् वरदाम् मातरम्। वन्दे मातरम्।

:::

:::

## The National Flag 🇮🇳 (The Tricolor)


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

- Saffron (Kesari): representing courage and sacrifice.

- White: peace and truth.

- Green: faith and chivalry

- Chakra of navy blue

:::

::: {.column}

- Design adopted on 22 July 1947

- Flag Code of India 2002 regulates flat's use and display.

- Prevention of Improper Use Act, 1950 & the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

:::

:::

> River Ganga
